Arachnids.Spider: All spiders are arachnids, with eight legs and two body segments. Most make silk, which is stronger than steel by weight.
Arachnids.Scorpion: One of the oldest land animals, with fossils dating back over 400 million years. Many glow blue-green under UV light.
Arachnids.Tick: Ticks are arachnids, not insects. After hatching, they need blood meals at each stage of life to grow.
Arachnids.Mite: Mites are among the most diverse arachnids, mostly microscopic. Some, like dust mites, live in homes and eat shed skin.
Arachnids.Tarantula: A big hairy spider. Many New World species flick irritating hairs from their abdomens as a defence.
Arachnids.Black widow: A venomous spider, named for the female's habit of sometimes eating the male. A red hourglass marks her underside.
Arachnids.Wolf spider: A hunting spider that doesn't build webs. Mothers carry the egg sac and later carry hundreds of babies on their backs.
Arachnids.Camel spider: Neither a camel nor a true spider; it's a solifuge, a distinct arachnid group, found in deserts and known for its speed.
Arachnids.Brown recluse: A venomous spider with a violin-shaped mark on its back. It is shy and bites mostly when pressed against skin.
Arachnids.Ant: An insect with six legs and three body sections. Unlike arachnids, ants have antennae.
Arachnids.Centipede: A myriapod, not an arachnid. It has a pair of legs on each body segment and antennae.
Arachnids.Millipede: A myriapod with four legs per segment, so many more legs than arachnids' eight. It has antennae.
Arachnids.Crab: A crustacean with a hard shell and ten legs. Crustaceans have antennae, which arachnids lack.
Arachnids.Lobster: A crustacean, closer to insects than spiders. It has two pairs of antennae, which arachnids don't.
Arachnids.Beetle: An insect with six legs, antennae and hard wing covers. Arachnids have eight legs and no antennae or wings.
Arachnids.Cricket: An insect with six legs. It chirps by rubbing its wings together, and some species hear through knees.
Arachnids.Silverfish: A wingless insect with six legs and antennae, so it is not an arachnid, though it looks like a creepy crawler.
Arachnids.Woodlouse: A land crustacean, so closer to a shrimp than a spider. It breathes with gill-like structures, which is why it needs damp spots.
Arachnids.Praying mantis: An insect with six legs, and it can turn its head 180 degrees. It looks predatory like a spider but is not one.
Arachnids.Earwig: An insect with pincers at the rear, which are sometimes mistaken for a scorpion's. It has six legs and antennae.
Arachnids.Stick insect: An insect, famous for camouflage that mimics twigs. Some species can reproduce without mating.
Arachnids.Dragonfly: An insect with large compound eyes and four wings. Six legs and antennae set it apart from arachnids.
Arachnids.Wasp: An insect with six legs and a narrow waist. Unlike most arachnids, its life cycle includes a larval stage.
Arachnids.Shrimp: A crustacean, not an arachnid. It has antennae, and comes from a different branch of the arthropod family.

Things found in a beehive.Queen bee: Queen bees can lay up to about 2,000 eggs in a day. Her pheromones keep the colony cohesive, and she can live for years.
Things found in a beehive.Drone: Drones are male bees that do no foraging or defence. Their sole job is to mate, and they die doing it. In autumn the colony evicts the rest.
Things found in a beehive.Worker bee: Worker bees are all female, and they do nearly everything. A worker makes only about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in her life.
Things found in a beehive.Honeycomb: Honeycomb cells are hexagons, the shape that stores the most with the least wax. Bees build it from wax their bodies secrete.
Things found in a beehive.Honey: Honey never spoils, and edible jars have turned up in ancient Egyptian tombs. Bees fan it with their wings to drive off moisture.
Things found in a beehive.Pollen: Pollen is the protein source for bees, packed onto their hind legs in pellets. Honeybees mix it with nectar into 'bee bread' for larvae.
Things found in a beehive.Beeswax: Beeswax is secreted from glands on a worker's abdomen in tiny flakes. Bees must eat several kilos of honey to produce one kilo of wax.
Things found in a beehive.Larvae: Larvae are the white, legless grubs in the hive's cells. Nurse bees feed them so frequently that they're visited thousands of times a day.
Things found in a beehive.Royal jelly: Royal jelly is a protein-rich secretion fed to all young larvae. Only a larva fed it exclusively becomes a queen.
Things found in a beehive.Propolis: Propolis is bee glue, made from tree resins. Bees use it to seal gaps, and its antimicrobial properties help keep the hive clean.
Things found in a beehive.Nectar: Nectar is a sugary liquid collected from flowers. Bees carry it in a special honey stomach and turn it into honey by evaporation.
Things found in a beehive.Brood: Brood means the eggs, larvae and pupae in the hive. Bees keep the brood nest at about 35 degrees Celsius, almost human-warm.
Things found in a beehive.Silk: Silkworms, not bees, produce silk. A single cocoon is made of one continuous thread that can be up to about 1,000 metres long.
Things found in a beehive.Spider web: Spider webs are made of silk, and by weight it's stronger than steel. Spiders are not found in beehives, as bees quickly tackle intruders.
Things found in a beehive.Ink: Squid and octopuses release ink as a defence. Dissolved in water, it forms a cloud that can also numb a predator's sense of smell.
Things found in a beehive.Pearl: Pearls form inside oysters when an irritant gets lodged. Layers of nacre then build up, which can take years.
Things found in a beehive.Milk: Milk is made by mammals, and bees aren't mammals. The only 'milk' in a hive is royal jelly, which is not milk in biology's sense.
Things found in a beehive.Acorn: Acorns are the fruit of oak trees. Oaks may produce millions across a lifetime, and jays and squirrels plant many by forgetting them.
Things found in a beehive.Feather: Feathers are unique to birds and some dinosaurs. A bird's body can bear thousands of them, and they're replaced by moulting.
Things found in a beehive.Antler: Antlers are bone that deer shed and regrow every year. They can grow up to about an inch a day, among the fastest tissue growth in mammals.
Things found in a beehive.Krill: Krill are tiny shrimp-like crustaceans that live in the ocean. Their total mass in the Southern Ocean may exceed that of humans.
Things found in a beehive.Chrysalis: A chrysalis is a butterfly's pupa, in which the caterpillar dissolves and rebuilds itself. Bees pupate too, but sealed in wax cells, not chrysalises.
Things found in a beehive.Guano: Guano is bird or bat droppings, collected for fertiliser. In the 1800s it was so valuable that nations fought over guano islands.
Things found in a beehive.Termite: Termites build vast mounds and are not bees. Their closest relatives are in fact cockroaches, not ants or bees.

Botanically berries (really!).Banana: Bananas are berries botanically, and the plant is a giant herb, not a tree, since its 'trunk' is just tightly wrapped leaf bases.
Botanically berries (really!).Grape: Grapes are berries, and their skin carries a natural yeast-friendly bloom, which is why they ferment so easily into wine.
Botanically berries (really!).Tomato: A tomato is a berry that grows from a single flower ovary, and a US Supreme Court case in 1893 ruled it a vegetable for tariff purposes.
Botanically berries (really!).Blueberry: Blueberries are true berries, and their blue is partly an illusion produced by the waxy coating, since the skin pigment is closer to dark purple.
Botanically berries (really!).Avocado: Avocado is a single-seeded berry, and the rough-skinned Hass type descends from one tree that a mailman grew in California in the 1920s.
Botanically berries (really!).Kiwi: Kiwi fruit is a berry, and it came from China, where it was known as the Chinese gooseberry, before New Zealand renamed it.
Botanically berries (really!).Eggplant: Eggplants are berries, relatives of tomatoes and potatoes, and their flesh holds many tiny edible seeds.
Botanically berries (really!).Cranberry: Cranberries are true berries, and their air pockets let them float, which is how bogs are flooded for harvest.
Botanically berries (really!).Chili pepper: Chili peppers are berries, and their heat comes from capsaicin, which birds can't feel so they spread the seeds.
Botanically berries (really!).Gooseberry: Gooseberries are true berries with a translucent striped skin, and they were once banned in parts of the US to protect pine trees from blister rust.
Botanically berries (really!).Persimmon: Persimmons are berries, and an unripe astringent type can pucker your mouth because of tannins until it softens.
Botanically berries (really!).Guava: Guavas are true berries, and they pack more vitamin C per fruit than an orange.
Botanically berries (really!).Strawberry: Strawberries aren't berries: the red flesh is a swollen stem base, and the real fruits are the tiny seeds on its surface.
Botanically berries (really!).Raspberry: Raspberries are clusters of tiny drupelets, each with a seed, so they're an aggregate fruit, not a true berry.
Botanically berries (really!).Blackberry: Blackberries are an aggregate of drupelets, so despite their name and look, botanists don't count them as true berries.
Botanically berries (really!).Mulberry: Mulberries are multiple fruits, formed from a whole cluster of flowers fused together, so not true berries.
Botanically berries (really!).Cherry: Cherries are drupes, stone fruits with a single hard pit, so they're not berries botanically.
Botanically berries (really!).Apple: Apples are pomes, a fruit type where the flesh grows from the flower tube around the core, not berries.
Botanically berries (really!).Peach: Peaches are drupes, with a hard stone surrounding the seed, which excludes them from the berry class.
Botanically berries (really!).Plum: Plums are drupes, with a hard pit, so they're stone fruits, not true berries.
Botanically berries (really!).Mango: Mangoes are drupes, with a large flat stone inside, which is one reason they aren't botanical berries.
Botanically berries (really!).Pear: Pears are pomes, like apples, and unlike most fruit they ripen best off the tree.
Botanically berries (really!).Fig: A fig is not a berry: it's an inverted flower cluster with the flowers hidden inside, and it's a syconium.
Botanically berries (really!).Pineapple: A pineapple is a multiple fruit formed from many flowers fused together, not a berry.

Gin cocktails.Negroni: Equal parts gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth. Legend says Count Camillo Negroni asked a Florence bartender in 1919 to strengthen his Americano.
Gin cocktails.Gin and tonic: Born with British soldiers in India, who mixed bitter quinine tonic, a malaria preventive, with gin to make it palatable.
Gin cocktails.Tom Collins: Named for a fictional bartender, John Collins; it's gin, lemon, sugar, and soda. Early recipes used Old Tom gin, a slightly sweeter style.
Gin cocktails.Gimlet: Gin and lime cordial. British Navy surgeon Thomas Gimlette is said to have pushed it as a way to get sailors to drink their vitamin C against scurvy.
Gin cocktails.French 75: Gin, lemon, sugar, and Champagne, named for a rapid-fire French field gun of World War I because of its kick.
Gin cocktails.Aviation: Gin, maraschino, lemon, and crème de violette, giving a sky-blue colour. The violet liqueur was hard to find for decades, so many bars dropped it.
Gin cocktails.Bramble: A modern British classic invented by Dick Bradsell in London in 1984, with blackberry liqueur drizzled over crushed ice like a bramble thicket.
Gin cocktails.Singapore Sling: Created around 1915 at Raffles Hotel in Singapore; the original was pink, with cherry liqueur and pineapple, and was meant to look like juice.
Gin cocktails.Gin fizz: Gin, lemon, sugar and soda, shaken then topped with fizz. The Ramos version needs a famously long shake, reportedly around twelve minutes, by hand.
Gin cocktails.Last Word: Equal parts gin, green Chartreuse, maraschino, and lime, from Detroit Athletic Club circa 1915. It was forgotten until a Seattle bartender revived it in 2004.
Gin cocktails.Bee's Knees: A Prohibition-era gin, lemon, and honey cocktail. Honey masked the harsh taste of bootleg bathtub gin.
Gin cocktails.Clover Club: Gin, lemon, raspberry syrup, and egg white, named for a Philadelphia gentlemen's club. The egg white gives its frothy pink head.
Gin cocktails.Mojito: A trap: white rum, mint, lime, sugar, and soda make a Cuban rum classic. It is not a gin drink, though a gin version, the Southside, exists.
Gin cocktails.Daiquiri: Rum, lime and sugar, named for a Cuban mining town. Hemingway's version used grapefruit and no sugar, which he drank in Havana's El Floridita.
Gin cocktails.Margarita: Tequila, triple sec, and lime. Many origin stories claim it, but none is certain; it is Mexico's best-known cocktail, not a gin one.
Gin cocktails.Cosmopolitan: Vodka, cranberry, lime, and triple sec; the pink drink made famous by Sex and the City. Vodka, not gin, is its base.
Gin cocktails.Moscow mule: Vodka, ginger beer, and lime, traditionally in a copper mug. It was partly a marketing stunt in the 1940s to sell vodka in America.
Gin cocktails.Old Fashioned: Whiskey, sugar, bitters, and an orange peel; arguably the original cocktail. Whiskey, not gin, anchors it.
Gin cocktails.Manhattan: Rye or bourbon with sweet vermouth and bitters, linked to a New York club. Its base is whiskey, not gin.
Gin cocktails.Piña colada: Rum, coconut cream, and pineapple, Puerto Rico's national drink since 1978. The name means strained pineapple, and rum is its base.
Gin cocktails.Mai tai: Rum, orgeat, lime, and orange curaçao. Trader Vic claimed to invent it in 1944; 'Maita'i' is Tahitian for 'good'. Rum, not gin.
Gin cocktails.Whiskey sour: Whiskey, lemon, and sugar, often with egg white. It is a whiskey classic and the base is not gin.
Gin cocktails.Bloody Mary: Vodka and tomato juice, not gin; the name nods to Mary I of England. Its gin-based predecessor, the Bucket of Blood, never caught on.
Gin cocktails.Paloma: Tequila, grapefruit soda, and lime. It is Mexico's most popular tequila mixed drink, rather than gin.

Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Hawaii: Mauna Kea, measured from the seafloor, is taller than Everest, and the islands are the tops of volcanoes rising from the ocean floor.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Tahiti: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia, and the painter Gauguin spent years there.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Fiji: Fiji is made of over 300 islands, and kava, a mildly numbing drink, is central to its ceremonies.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Samoa: Samoa moved across the International Date Line in 2011, skipping an entire day, December 30.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Tonga: Tonga's monarchy dates to the 1800s, and it's the only Pacific island kingdom never to lose its sovereignty to a colonial power.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Guam: Guam is a US territory, and close to the Mariana Trench, the deepest known place in the ocean.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Bora Bora: Bora Bora's central peak, Mount Otemanu, is an extinct volcano ringed by a lagoon and coral reef.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Easter Island: Easter Island's nearly 900 moai statues were carved by the Rapa Nui people, and many were moved across the island by unknown methods.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Galápagos: The Galápagos finches and tortoises helped to inspire Darwin's thinking about evolution; the islands belong to Ecuador.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.New Caledonia: New Caledonia is surrounded by one of the world's largest lagoons, and its crows are among the best tool users of any bird.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Vanuatu: On Pentecost Island in Vanuatu, men leap from tall towers with vines tied to their ankles, the origin of bungee jumping.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Palau: Palau has a lake full of non-stinging jellyfish and was among the first nations to make a shark sanctuary.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Maldives: The Maldives lie in the Indian Ocean, and are the lowest-lying country on Earth, averaging about 1.5 meters above sea level.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Mauritius: Mauritius, home of the extinct dodo, is in the Indian Ocean, far from the Pacific.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Seychelles: The Seychelles are in the Indian Ocean, and some of the oldest granite islands in the ocean.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Madagascar: Madagascar is in the Indian Ocean, and about 90 percent of its wildlife, including lemurs, exists nowhere else.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Zanzibar: Zanzibar is in the Indian Ocean off Tanzania, famed for its Stone Town and spices.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Bermuda: Bermuda is in the Atlantic, and the Bermuda Triangle's reputation is mostly legend.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Barbados: Barbados is the easternmost Caribbean island, in the Atlantic, so it is not a Pacific island.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Canary Islands: The Canaries are in the Atlantic, off the Moroccan coast, with Mount Teide the highest peak in Spain.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Azores: The Azores are in the Atlantic Ocean, midway between Europe and North America.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Iceland: Iceland straddles the Mid-Atlantic Ridge in the Atlantic, where two tectonic plates are pulling apart.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Sri Lanka: Sri Lanka is in the Indian Ocean, and it was called Ceylon until 1972.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean.Bahamas: The Bahamas are Atlantic islands, and the first land Columbus saw in the Americas was probably there.

Cities in Italy.Rome: Rome is called the Eternal City, and the Colosseum there once held about 50,000 spectators.
Cities in Italy.Milan: Milan is Italy's fashion and design capital, and La Scala opera house and Leonardo's Last Supper are both there.
Cities in Italy.Naples: Naples is where pizza was born, and Vesuvius looms over the city.
Cities in Italy.Venice: Venice is built on over 100 small islands and is linked by about 400 bridges, with canals instead of streets.
Cities in Italy.Florence: Florence was the center of the Renaissance, and the Medici family there funded Michelangelo and Leonardo.
Cities in Italy.Turin: Turin is the home of Fiat and the Shroud of Turin, and it hosted the 2006 Winter Olympics.
Cities in Italy.Bologna: Bologna has the world's oldest university in continuous operation, from 1088, and the original ragù.
Cities in Italy.Genoa: Genoa is the birthplace of Christopher Columbus, and the home of pesto.
Cities in Italy.Verona: Verona is the setting for Romeo and Juliet, and its Roman arena still stages opera.
Cities in Italy.Palermo: Palermo is the capital of Sicily, with Arab-Norman palaces and a lively street food scene.
Cities in Italy.Pisa: Pisa's tower started to lean while it was being built, because it was on soft ground, and it took centuries to finish.
Cities in Italy.Siena: Siena holds the Palio, a wild horse race around its main square, run twice each summer.
Cities in Italy.Trieste: Trieste is an Italian port on the border with Slovenia, known for its coffee culture and for Joyce's years there.
Cities in Italy.Nice: Nice is in France, on the Riviera, and was part of Italy until 1860.
Cities in Italy.Monaco: Monaco is a city-state, the second-smallest country in the world, and not part of Italy.
Cities in Italy.Marseille: Marseille is in France, and was founded by Greek traders around 600 BC.
Cities in Italy.Lugano: Lugano is in the Italian-speaking part of Switzerland, so people speak Italian but live in Swiss territory.
Cities in Italy.Ljubljana: Ljubljana is the capital of Slovenia, and has a dragon as its symbol.
Cities in Italy.Split: Split is a Croatian city, built within the palace of the Roman emperor Diocletian.
Cities in Italy.Dubrovnik: Dubrovnik is a Croatian walled city on the Adriatic, and a filming location for Game of Thrones.
Cities in Italy.Valletta: Valletta is the capital of Malta, and one of the smallest capitals in the EU.
Cities in Italy.Barcelona: Barcelona is in Spain, and is the home of Gaudí's architecture.
Cities in Italy.Athens: Athens is the capital of Greece, and its Parthenon dates to the 5th century BC.
Cities in Italy.San Marino: San Marino is an independent republic inside Italy, said to be the world's oldest, founded in 301.

Lakes of Africa.Victoria: Africa's largest lake by area, shared by Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya, is the main source of the White Nile.
Lakes of Africa.Tanganyika: It is the world's longest freshwater lake and the second deepest, after Baikal.
Lakes of Africa.Malawi: It holds more fish species than any other lake, hundreds of colorful cichlids found nowhere else.
Lakes of Africa.Chad: Lake Chad has lost around 90 percent of its area since the 1960s, due to drought and water use.
Lakes of Africa.Turkana: Kenya's Jade Sea is the world's largest permanent desert lake, with a greenish tint from algae.
Lakes of Africa.Volta: This lake in Ghana was formed by the Akosombo Dam in 1965, and it is one of the world's biggest reservoirs by area.
Lakes of Africa.Kariba: Zambia and Zimbabwe share this lake, created by damming the Zambezi, and it is one of the largest reservoirs by volume.
Lakes of Africa.Albert: On the Uganda-Congo border in the Rift Valley, it is fed by the Victoria Nile.
Lakes of Africa.Edward: This Rift Valley lake on the border of Uganda and DR Congo is known for its hippos and fish.
Lakes of Africa.Kivu: This lake on the Rwanda and DR Congo border holds huge amounts of dissolved methane gas.
Lakes of Africa.Titicaca: A trap. This is in the Andes of Peru and Bolivia, at 3,800 m the world's highest large navigable lake.
Lakes of Africa.Baikal: Siberia's lake is the deepest on Earth, and holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water.
Lakes of Africa.Geneva: The lake at the western end of Switzerland is shared with France, and Geneva sits on its shore.
Lakes of Africa.Como: Italy's Alpine lake is Y-shaped and over 400 m deep.
Lakes of Africa.Superior: The largest Great Lake in North America is the largest freshwater lake by surface area in the world.
Lakes of Africa.Loch Ness: Scotland's lake, more famous for its monster, holds more water than all English and Welsh lakes.
Lakes of Africa.Garda: Italy's largest lake lies at the foot of the Alps.
Lakes of Africa.Tahoe: Straddling California and Nevada, it is about 500 m deep and famously clear.
Lakes of Africa.Balaton: Hungary's lake is the largest in Central Europe and is shallow, so it warms quickly.
Lakes of Africa.Ladoga: Russia's lake near St Petersburg is the largest in Europe.
Lakes of Africa.Eyre: This Australian lake is usually a dry salt pan, and it fills only after rare floods.
Lakes of Africa.Constance: Germany, Switzerland and Austria all border this lake, whose borders have never been formally agreed.
Lakes of Africa.Great Salt Lake: Utah's lake is saltier than the sea and has been shrinking in recent years.
Lakes of Africa.Winnipeg: One of Canada's largest lakes, it lies in Manitoba.
